# Front sway bar link wear and bushings

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Examine front sway bar brackets for worn bushings and inspect links where ends connect. [t2019]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Examine the front sway bar located along the front of the cross member.
2. Check the two brackets holding the bar for worn bushings that cause clunks.

_Procedure reported by [t2019]._

## Tips & gotchas

- Inspect the ends of the sway bar where links connect to the lower control arm (LCA). [t2019]
- Look at the tops of these links, as they tend to get worn down or whittled off. [t2019]
- Note that a broken link can be hard to spot because the two pieces rest on each other when parked. [t2019]
